Keysight Technologies Inc reported third quarter revenue of 1.85 billion dollars, up 36.54 percent from a year earlier [D1]. Net income was 397 million dollars, up 107.85 percent from a year earlier, with a gross margin of 65.87 percent and a net margin of 21.51 percent [D1]. The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of 1.345 billion dollars and the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of 501 million dollars [D1]. For the fourth quarter, management guided revenue of 1.93 billion dollars to 1.95 billion dollars and earnings per share of 3.34 dollars to 3.40 dollars on a diluted share count of 172 million [D1].

The market debate centers on whether demand can be converted into revenue given supply chain constraints [D3]. Management said the supply environment is less flexible today than a year ago and that supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue [D3]. Management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply, and that the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear [D3]. Management also cautioned that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat [D3]. Analysts questioned the sustainability of demand and fulfillment, including whether guidance is capped by supply [D3].

Management raised its outlook for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year, and expects fourth quarter orders to be slightly up from the third quarter [D3]. To manage supply, management is working with suppliers to deconstrain the supply chain [D3]. The integration of recent acquisitions is largely complete, including systems migrations, one quarter ahead of schedule [D3]. Management said supply will be a governor of its ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters [D3].
